result:
Turbonomic can help Unilever leverage AI for multi-cloud observability by providing a unified, AI-driven platform that automates the management of complex, multi-cloud environments. It uses AI to analyze real-time data from various cloud providers, identifying performance bottlenecks and cost inefficiencies. This allows Unilever to proactively manage their infrastructure, ensuring optimal performance and cost-effectiveness across all clouds.

The difference between Turbonomic and native tools from GCP, AWS, and Azure lies in their scope and capabilities. Native tools are specific to their respective cloud providers and may not offer a unified view or automated management across multiple clouds. Turbonomic, on the other hand, provides a single pane of glass for all clouds, offering cross-cloud visibility and automated remediation. It also uses AI to predict and prevent issues before they occur, whereas native tools may be more reactive.

function.name: get_weather_forecast
function.description: Retrieves the weather forecast for a specified location and date range. The forecast includes temperature, precipitation, and wind speed. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which the weather forecast is requested, in the format of 'City, Country' (e.g., 'London, UK').

start_date.description: The start date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-01').

end_date.description: The end date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-07').

units.description: The unit system in which to return the weather forecast data.

include_details.description: Specifies whether to include detailed forecast information such as humidity and visibility.
